posts.author: PlayBoxTech
posts.body:
Hi all,
New to making an RPG, I was curious when you start making one do you make the "golden path" first? And then go back and add the side quests?
Thanks

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
It is definitely a good approach, as, if you need to alter your scope and cut stuff, it will be optional content. Having the main storyline done, is a big milestone. In my current project, I like to go on chronologically, so I added every feature when I needed it. But still I'm backtracking from time to time to add more side content to the early game. I guess it depends on the game and what is useful for you to continue developing.
My advice would be to not spend too much time on things you'll change later again anyway. To name two examples, I spend little to no time on balanced battles yet, as the balancing will be done in the very end. I already know, all the spells, dmg formulas and even features might and will change, so it doesn't matter right now. Also I didn't implement a menu yet, as I will see in the end what features I'll actually have to cover.
Also, motivation is somewhat unpredictable. You might have fun today doing your main quest, but tomorrow, you're inspired to add a side quest. Don't hold yourself back, just do it. I caught myself quite some times, procrastinating by adding features, that I was procrastinating for weeks on.

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
PlayBoxTech said:
do you make the "golden path" first? And then go back and add the side quests?
Click to expand...
pretty much, yeah.
people are badly accustomed to [the product RPG game] having all these modern features like crafting, romancing, recruiting, influencing, etc... but *the game* itself only exists thanks to the story behind it.
*THE* story is always the first thing you have to work on.... otherwise you're just making a generic [product RPG]
*AN* RPG as such isn't required to have
all these modern features
as listed, so, don't consider side-quests as a must, nor even the starting point for design.
